- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at +5% above prior high.
- If official supply net is strongly bearish (net < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside; add 2–5% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67); model often fails to revert; force 30d forecast to align with 18d moving average if sentiment < 0.5.
- If 30d forecast is rising steadily (slope >0.01) and sentiment is flat or bearish, model is overconfident; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% if supply net is negative.
- For auctions with high supply net (e.g., net > -10), model often underestimates price drop; add 1–3% downward adjustment to 30d forecast if auction is within next 7 days.
